title: Deploying Python Applications
description: Learn how to prepare, package, and deploy Python applications to different environments for production use.

lessons.title: Introduction to Deployment
lessons.content: Deployment is the process of making your application available for users by moving it from development to production.

lessons.title: Preparing Your Application for Deployment
lessons.content: Clean code, remove debug prints, handle configuration via environment variables, and ensure dependencies are listed.

lessons.title: Packaging Python Applications
lessons.content:
Use tools like setuptools to create distributable packages:
```python
from setuptools import setup

setup(
    name='myapp',
    version='1.0',
    packages=['myapp'],
    install_requires=['requests'],
)
```

lessons.title: Deploying Web Apps on Heroku
lessons.content:
Steps to deploy:
- Create Procfile
- Install Heroku CLI
- git push to Heroku
Example Procfile:
```
web: gunicorn app:app
```

lessons.title: Using Docker for Deployment
lessons.content:
Docker packages apps with their environment:
```dockerfile
FROM python:3.9
WORKDIR /app
COPY . .
RUN pip install -r requirements.txt
CMD ["python", "app.py"]
```

lessons.title: Deploying to Cloud Platforms (AWS, GCP, Azure)
lessons.content: Cloud providers offer scalable hosting. Understand services like AWS Elastic Beanstalk, Google App Engine, or Azure App Services.

lessons.title: Environment Variables and Configuration
lessons.content: Store sensitive data like API keys securely using environment variables instead of hardcoding.

lessons.title: Setting Up a Production Database
lessons.content: Use managed databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL) for reliability. Configure connection strings securely.

lessons.title: Monitoring and Logging in Production
lessons.content: Monitor app health and errors using tools like Sentry or CloudWatch. Logs help debug issues post-deployment.

lessons.title: Rolling Back Deployments and Version Control
lessons.content: Use version control and deployment strategies to revert to previous stable versions if needed.
